prose.def: Describing someone or something as strong, powerful, and able to exert force.
prose.article: κραταιός means strong or mighty, describing power and the ability to exert force. It appears only once in the Byzantine New Testament, at 1 Peter 5:6, where it speaks of God's "mighty" hand, and translators agree on "mighty" 100% of the time. It is far more common in the Septuagint (54 times in 18 books), where it usually renders the Hebrew word for "strong" (חָזָק, 26 times); interestingly, the same word turns up in magical papyri addressing "mighty gods."
prose.caution: With only one New Testament occurrence, the measured sense rests on thin evidence, though the Septuagint and lexicons agree on "strong, mighty."
